theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.eval_transport
premises: Two supplied partial algebras over the existing finite structural Tree
A total carrier map h
Hom equations for every seed, unary operation and ordered binary operation, as equalities of complete Option results
theorems.conclusion: Evaluation of every finite Tree commutes with Option.map h.
theorems.limits: Single-carrier algebra; no intrinsic typed-signature calculus, linguistic adequacy, binder semantics, or correspondence between evaluation definedness and grammar Certified is assumed or established.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.eval_definedness_iff
premises: The same partial-algebra Hom equations
theorems.conclusion: Source evaluation is none exactly when target evaluation is none for the same finite Tree.
theorems.limits: Undefinedness is relative to the supplied operations; it is not a judgment that an Arabic expression has no meaning.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.observed_eval_preserved
premises: Hom equations
Independently supplied source and target observation functions
Explicit Faithful equation for every carrier value and query
theorems.conclusion: Optional observed evaluation results are exactly equal for each declared query.
theorems.limits: Homomorphism alone is insufficient. Adequacy and contextual completeness of the observation family remain separate obligations; world truth is not concluded.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.unique_decoder_on_image_iff
premises: Arbitrary total encode : X -> R and query : X -> Y
theorems.conclusion: A decoder correct and unique on the image of encode exists iff query is constant on every encoding fiber.
theorems.limits: Decoder restricted to the image, including the empty-domain case. Existence may use standard Classical.choice; no executable decoder extraction or human cognition claim. Reuses the existing ArabicCoverage collision boundary instead of duplicating its impossibility theorem.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.observations_exact_with_transport
premises: Independently supplied domain and reference relation
Existing ArabicCoverage.ExactWithin for the source recognizer
Target relation exactly equals the transported image of all recognized source readings within the domain
Independent Faithful observation equation
theorems.conclusion: The target relation of whole observation functions is exact relative to the reference observation relation on that domain.
theorems.limits: Does not establish parser completeness, linguistic reference adequacy or all-Arabic coverage. A whole observation function belongs to one reading; existential projections are not independently recombined.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.same_observations_iff_query_eq
premises: Two typed Packets
theorems.conclusion: Bidirectional membership of the complete Observation tuples is equivalent to equality of the installed query predicates.
theorems.limits: The query preserves tagged resolved arguments, polarity, tense, voice, force, scope, convention, source time and place. It is not the entire meaning of Arabic.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.local_violation_none_iff
premises: A typed DecodedCase
theorems.conclusion: The local diagnostic scan returns none iff exact source binding, exact source context and the complete observation set are preserved.
theorems.limits: The adapter actually supplies decoded from the payload. This theorem does not prove JSON parsing refinement.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.collision_for_none_iff
premises: A finite supplied list of typed DecodedCase values and one first case
theorems.conclusion: The collision scan returns none iff every list case sharing the complete transported string has the same original observation set.
theorems.limits: Full string equality, not a hash or label, determines fibers. This says nothing about unsupplied cases.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.first_violation_none_iff
premises: A finite supplied list of typed DecodedCase values
theorems.conclusion: The actual native semantic scan returns none iff the independently stated FiniteContract holds: all fibers are compatible and every case is locally preserved.
theorems.limits: Semantic decisions follow complete strict decoding. Wire validity, resource limits and case-ID uniqueness are independently enforced by the adapter.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.finite_check_exact
premises: A finite supplied list of typed DecodedCase values
theorems.conclusion: The Boolean check is true iff FiniteContract holds.
theorems.limits: The mathematical contract is vacuously true on an empty list; the native wire parser rejects empty case and reading arrays, so this cannot certify a positive textual interpretation.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.finite_check_preserves_each
premises: The finite check accepts
A case belongs to the supplied list
theorems.conclusion: That case preserves its complete binding, complete source context and joint observation set.
theorems.limits: Readings in authored mode are modeling premises. The theorem does not acquire them from arbitrary natural text or authenticate their source.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.finite_check_fiber_compatible
premises: The finite check accepts
theorems.conclusion: FiberCompatible holds for the full-string encoder and installed query on the subtype of supplied cases.
theorems.limits: The source domain is precisely the supplied finite subtype. Sample agreement is not generalized to an open domain.

theorems.name: Nabt.MeaningPreservation.finite_check_decoder_on_image
premises: The finite check accepts
theorems.conclusion: A correct unique query decoder exists on the image of the supplied finite payload encoder.
theorems.limits: Mathematical existence/uniqueness theorem, distinct from the native adapter's actual JSON decoder. Does not prove universal ontology decoding, human agreement, or external truth.
